cases.input: 모든 사람은 죽는다. 소크라테스는 사람이다. 따라서 소크라테스는 죽는다.
cases.form: Barbara syllogism: All M are P; S is M; therefore S is P
cases.verdict_summary: Valid universal-instantiation syllogism with true premises; therefore sound. No fallacies.

cases.input: 모든 새는 난다. 펭귄은 새다. 따라서 펭귄은 난다.

premises.basis: counterexamples exist: penguins, ostriches, kiwis are flightless birds

cases.form: All M are P; S is M; therefore S is P (same valid form as B1)

fallacies.why: Premise is empirically false; the form is valid so the conclusion follows from premises, but a false premise makes the argument unsound.

cases.verdict_summary: Form is valid (identical to B1) but premise 1 is false, so the argument is unsound. Error = false premise. Validity and soundness correctly separated.

cases.input: 비가 오면 땅이 젖는다. 땅이 젖었다. 따라서 비가 왔다.
cases.form: P -> Q; Q; therefore P  (INVALID conditional form)

fallacies.why: The ground could be wet for other reasons (sprinkler, flood, dew). Q does not entail P; this is the formal fallacy of affirming the consequent.

cases.verdict_summary: Invalid: affirming the consequent. Conclusion does not follow even if premises are true; soundness is moot (undetermined) because validity fails.
